text: We tried to reproduce the “rapacious spectral sequence” from the first lecture of the course “Coloured metalibraries. The mind of space” (R. Mikhailov, 2 September 2016): to compute the $E^2$ page of the coloured metalibrary and to apply to it the rule “eat yourself as fast as possible, constrained only by colour”.

The coloured $E^2$ page of the metalibrary is computed up to $\pi_{150}$. The colour turned out to be the number of Bocksteins (the $Q$-weight) in the unstable Ext; this was checked cell by cell against a direct computation in the lambda algebra up to $\pi_{75}$ and selectively up to $\pi_{85}$ (method and checks).
The colours of the sandwiches and the Toda elements run 3 4 4 5 5 6 …, as stated in the lecture (classes).
The rapacious rule with colour $+1$ agrees with Toda's table for all $n\le48$, including $\pi_{44}=0$. The boundary is exactly the stems $k<46$, the ones Toda determined in 1967.

The rule reproduces the predictions of the lecture: $\pi_{48}=0$, and there is 3-torsion for all $49\le n\le149$; in $\pi_{71}$ there are two copies of $\mathbb Z/3$ under one of the orders of eating (comparison).

Beyond $\pi_{48}$ the rule disagrees with Toda's 2003 table ($\pi_{49}$, $\pi_{50}$, $\pi_{51}$, $\pi_{59}$, $\pi_{60}$, $\pi_{63}$, $\pi_{64}$, $\pi_{66}$, $\pi_{67}$, $\pi_{68}$, $\pi_{69}$, $\pi_{70}$, $\pi_{73}$, $\pi_{74}$, $\pi_{75}$, $\pi_{76}$, $\pi_{77}$, $\pi_{79}$, $\pi_{80}$), leaving more classes in every case. Toda has one copy in $\pi_{71}$ and zeros in $\pi_{51},\pi_{60},\pi_{67},\pi_{75},\pi_{76},\pi_{80}$ (our reading). For $\pi_{49}$–$\pi_{51}$, $\pi_{59}$, $\pi_{60}$ this is proved in a way that can be checked without trusting our program (verifiability). Almost all of the extra classes are removed by colour-preserving $d_5$'s, but not by all the allowed ones (differentials).
The rule does not determine the order of eating when a class can be both a target and a source; $\pi_{71}$, for instance, depends on it (differentials).

R. Mikhailov, lecture 1 of the course Tsvetnye metabiblioteki. Razum prostranstva (Coloured metalibraries. The mind of space), Chebyshev Laboratory, St. Petersburg State University, 2 September 2016, in Russian: YouTube.
S. O. Ivanov, R. Mikhailov, J. Wu, On nontriviality of homotopy groups of spheres, arXiv:1506.00952: the mod-$p$ lambda algebra.
H. Toda, Unstable 3-primary Homotopy Groups of Spheres, Econoinformatics 29 (2003): scan; H. Toda, Composition Methods in Homotopy Groups of Spheres, 1962.
The sseq project, program ext: github.com/JoeyBF/sseq: an independent computation of the unstable Ext.

ispacex/dimension-subrings: computations and Lean on dimension subgroups, the question $D_5(G)\subseteq\gamma_4(G)$ for groups. A companion to the paper of V. Ionin, R. Mikhailov and T. Petrov, Dimension subrings of Lie rings (arXiv:2610.02042), which proves the analogous inclusion for Lie rings. It is not about the metalibrary.
ispacex/cflint-fast-core (GitLab): a fast core for integral dimension subgroups $D_n(G)$ of finite $p$-groups (C/FLINT).

ispacex/meta-rapacious: the code of the recomputation: the lambda algebra, the $E^2$ of the metalibrary by colour (Python and Rust), the rapacious rule, the generator and the checkers of the certificates, the Lean project and the generator of this site (MIT license).
ispacex/metalibrary: the data and the pages of this site; the verification certificates are published as its release. The pages are built by the code in ispacex/meta-rapacious (verifiability).
